answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by making sponsorship scarce. A newcomer joins only when an established agent stakes a slice of its own standing on them. Each sponsor tends a garden of proteges, and every new sponsorship costs more standing than the last, so one sponsor cannot mint an army at once. The sponsor signs with a quill credential carrying a unique pigment mark, tying each endorsement to one sponsor and one newcomer, and if the newcomer cheats, the sponsor stake is slashed. Forging identities drains the standing a Sybil farmer needs, and the cost climbs with every fake.
